Blot detection coding

Gomes Lab. 264 papers for Rain. Rubric MV-1.0.

Read the Methods and the figure legends for this paper and decide how its western blots were detected. Choose exactly one.

  • Film: blots were exposed to X-ray or photographic film (developed, autoradiography), and no imager is named for blots.
  • Digital imager: chemiluminescent blots were captured on a camera or CCD imager, for example ChemiDoc, Amersham Imager or LAS, iBright, FluorChem, Fusion, G:BOX.
  • Fluorescent scanner: fluorescent or near-infrared secondary antibodies read on a fluorescence scanner, for example Odyssey CLx, Typhoon, Sapphire in fluorescence mode.
  • Chemiluminescent, capture not stated: ECL or a named HRP substrate is stated, but not how the signal was captured.
  • Mixed: more than one of film, digital imager and fluorescent scanner is named for western blots.
  • Not described: blot detection is not described, or the paper has no western blot.

A device named only for something else (a gel, an ELISA, a microscope) does not count. Tick No western blot in this paper when you see none at all, and choose Not described. Use the note for anything you were unsure about.

Keys 1 to 6 choose a class, and the arrow keys move between papers when you are not typing in the note. Enter your initials, then press Save to lab sheet whenever you stop, including when you finish. Each save sends everything coded so far, and you can keep working afterward. If a save cannot be confirmed, the sheet downloads a copy; send Benjamin that file.
